name: front_running_patterns
description: Missing slippage/deadline protection on swaps enabling sandwich/front-running attacks
question: The source file in `source` defines a Solidity function that performs a token swap or liquidity operation (e.g., calling an internal swap/exchange routine or transferring tokens based on a computed output amount) but does not accept or enforce a user-supplied minimum-output (slippage) parameter and/or does not enforce a deadline/timestamp check before executing, allowing an attacker to sandwich the transaction and force execution at a manipulated, unfavorable price.
criteria: Function performs a swap, exchange, or liquidity add/remove and computes an output/input amount internally
No parameter such as minAmountOut, minLiquidity, or minReceived is checked against the computed result before completing the operation
No deadline parameter or block.timestamp/expiry check is present to bound when the transaction can be executed
Absence of a revert/require statement comparing actual output to a minimum acceptable value
Function is externally/publicly callable and directly affects token transfer amounts or pricing
